sections.heading: Lead
Song information
sections.wikitext:
"The Way You Move" is credited to Big Boi, Sleepy Brown, and the song's producer, Carlton Mahone; Big Boi also does some co-production. Combining elements of [[Miami bass|bass music]], [[Atlanta]]-style [[southern hip hop]], and 1970s [[soul music]], "The Way You Move" is Big Boi's light-hearted dedication to women.

The song's instrumental track is punctuated with the prominent live [[horn section]] "Hornz Unlimited" of Atlanta reminiscent of [[Earth, Wind and Fire]], which features Sleepy Brown singing in style inspired by the work of [[Motown]] star [[Marvin Gaye]].
sections.text:
"The Way You Move" is credited to Big Boi, Sleepy Brown, and the song's producer, Carlton Mahone; Big Boi also does some co-production. Combining elements of bass music, Atlanta-style southern hip hop, and 1970s soul music, "The Way You Move" is Big Boi's light-hearted dedication to women.

The song's instrumental track is punctuated with the prominent live horn section "Hornz Unlimited" of Atlanta reminiscent of Earth, Wind and Fire, which features Sleepy Brown singing in style inspired by the work of Motown star Marvin Gaye.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The song's [[music video]], directed by [[Bryan Barber]], features Big Boi as the proprietor of a [[Wheel|rim]] shop. The video's performance shots eventually gravitate to other locations during the video's running time, featuring several young women who Big Boi, dressed in a pimp's suit, attempts to pick up.

The video features an appearance from [[Fonzworth Bentley]] and another from actress Ki Toy Johnson. "The Way You Move" music video was designed to be shown in tandem with the video for André 3000's "[[Hey Ya!]]". A long-form "The Way You Move/Hey Ya!" video combines both clips with a bridging sequence. The music video opens with Big Boi and Sleepy Brown pulling into a garage that specializes in automotive audio systems.<ref>Kaufman, Gil. [https://web.archive.org/web/20121106161838/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1479158/outkasts-hey-ya-ran-dre-into-ground.jhtml "Outkast's 'Hey Ya!' Clip Ran Andre 3000 Into The Ground: VMA Lens Recap"][[MTV News]]. September 19, 2003. Retrieved February 8, 2011.</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"The Way You Move" debuted at number 83 on the week ending September 27, 2003, a month after its release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hBEEAAAAMBAJ |title=September 27, 2003 ''Billboard'' Issue |date=September 27, 2003 | access-date=October 14, 2014}}</ref> It would later reach number two for eight consecutive weeks behind the group's other lead single "[[Hey Ya!]]".

It finally replaced "Hey Ya!" at number one on February 14, 2004, where it stayed for one week, which was the sixth time a recording act has replaced itself on the ''Billboard'' pop chart.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=February 14, 2004 |title=The Hot 100 Chart |magazine=Billboard |url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/2004-02-14 |access-date=May 28, 2021}}</ref> "The Way You Move" was ranked number five on the 2004 ''Billboard'' Year-End Chart. On the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart, "The Way You Move" peaked at number two (seven positions higher than "Hey Ya!"), and topped the [[Hot Rap Songs|Hot Rap Tracks]] chart.
sections.text:
"The Way You Move" debuted at number 83 on the week ending September 27, 2003, a month after its release. It would later reach number two for eight consecutive weeks behind the group's other lead single "Hey Ya!".

It finally replaced "Hey Ya!" at number one on February 14, 2004, where it stayed for one week, which was the sixth time a recording act has replaced itself on the Billboard pop chart. "The Way You Move" was ranked number five on the 2004 Billboard Year-End Chart. On the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart, "The Way You Move" peaked at number two (seven positions higher than "Hey Ya!"), and topped the Hot Rap Tracks chart.

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
* The song was featured and poked fun at in an episode of ''[[Chappelle's Show]]'', in a skit entitled "Making the Band", in which P. Diddy (played by Chappelle) is joined by his assistant, Fonzworth Bentley (played by Chappelle), who comes flying in using his umbrella as a parachute, just as Fonzworth does in "The Way You Move" music video.
* A heavily edited version of the song is featured in the console versions of ''[[Tiger Woods PGA Tour 2005]]'', and is a playable song in ''[[Shark Tale (video game)|Shark Tale]]''.
* The "Full Phatt Radio Mix" is featured on ''[[Dance Dance Revolution Universe 2]]''.
* A marching band performance of the song was included in the [[Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show]]<ref name=Esquire>{{cite web |last1=Holmes |first1=Dave |title=Revisiting the Justin Timberlake-Janet Jackson Wardrobe Malfunction, Minute by Minute |url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/music/a16020580/justin-timberlake-janet-jackson-super-bowl-halftime-show-wardrobe-malfunction/ |publisher=Esquire |access-date=February 6, 2020 |date=February 2, 2018}}</ref>
* Big Boi performed the song in the [[Super Bowl LIII halftime show]].

Earth, Wind & Fire: The Way You Move|date=2004|publisher=[[Arista Records]]}}</ref> The song reached No. 12 on both the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Contemporary Songs]] chart and [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] [[Smooth Jazz Songs]] chart. "The Way You Move" also reached No. 25 on the [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] [[Adult R&B Songs]] chart.<ref name="Billboard">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/earth-wind-fire/chart-history/asi/|title=Kenny G feat. Earth, Wind & Fire: The Way You Move (Adult Contemporary Songs)|website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref><ref name="Billboard1">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/earth-wind-fire/chart-history/jsi/|title=Kenny G featuring Earth, Wind & Fire: The Way You Move (Smooth Jazz Songs)|website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref><ref name="Billboard2">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/earth-wind-fire/chart-history/rba/|title=Kenny G featuring Earth, Wind & Fire: The Way You Move (Adult R&B Songs)|website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref>

In 2004, saxophonist Kenny G and Earth, Wind & Fire issued a cover of "The Way You Move" as a single on Arista Records. The song reached No. 12 on both the Billboard Adult Contemporary Songs chart and Billboard Smooth Jazz Songs chart. "The Way You Move" also reached No. 25 on the Billboard Adult R&B Songs chart.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.wikitext: "The Way You Move" appeared on Kenny G's 2004 LP ''[[At Last...The Duets Album]]'' and Earth, Wind & Fire's 2005 album ''[[Illumination (Earth, Wind & Fire album)|Illumination]]''.<ref>{{cite book|title=Kenny G: At Last...The Duets Album|date=2004|publisher=[[Arista Records]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: Illumination|date=2005|publisher=[[Sanctuary Records]]}}</ref>
sections.text: "The Way You Move" appeared on Kenny G's 2004 LP At Last...The Duets Album and Earth, Wind & Fire's 2005 album Illumination.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
[[People (magazine)|''People'']] called the tune a "polyrythmic party".<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Staff|url=https://people.com/archive/picks-and-pans-review-kenny-g-vol-63-no-3/|title=Picks and Pans Review: Kenny G|date=January 24, 2005|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419202345/https://people.com/archive/picks-and-pans-review-kenny-g-vol-63-no-3/|archive-date=April 19, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2025}}</ref> Matt Collar of [[Allmusic]] declared that "Earth, Wind & Fire pull a 'no brainer' on Outkast's 'The Way You Move.'"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/at-lastthe-duets-album-mw0000265749|title=Kenny G: At Last..The Duets Album|author=Collar, Matt|publisher=[[Allmusic]]|website=allmusic.com}}</ref> 
David Wild of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' said that this version "could go down as the funkiest song" in Kenny G's catalog.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/illumination-246864/|title=Earth, Wind & Fire: Illumination|date=November 28, 2005|author=Wild, David|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]}}</ref>
sections.text:
People called the tune a "polyrythmic party". Matt Collar of Allmusic declared that "Earth, Wind & Fire pull a 'no brainer' on Outkast's 'The Way You Move.'" 
David Wild of Rolling Stone said that this version "could go down as the funkiest song" in Kenny G's catalog.
